summary: Hand-written regex detectors for 13 template properties; those perfectly aligned with label in every sample form the candidate set. Corpus latent activations regressed on all properties give per-property latent shifts; dot with probe gradient gives per-property effects. Topic effect re-estimated in scored-logit space (label coefficient from a sample regression minus confound contributions); dependence = property effect / topic effect, thresholds 0.3 / 0.15. Two borderline properties settled with 2x2 topic-by-property template notes on true logits. Latents ranked by gradient x corpus shift, same sign as total, small topic contribution; probe 0 split 11/5 between two cues. Ablation on sample notes checked captured shift and latent-count saturation before submitting.

phases.purpose: Read task info, sample files and corpus notes to see the template structure.
Write 13 regex property detectors, check ~50% corpus splits, find the 8 properties perfectly confounded with label in all four samples.
Gradients for all probes, mean-pooled activations for the 384 corpus notes and all sample notes, base logits on sample notes.
Check that activation x gradient correlates with sample logits.
Multivariate corpus regression of activations on properties; dependence ratios with topic effect measured in activation x gradient space (later superseded).
Regress sample logits on label plus non-confounded properties; re-estimate topic effect in logit space; recompute dependence and use non-confounded properties as a calibration check.
2x2 topic-by-property template notes for the borderline properties (bullet on probe 0, exclamation on probe 3); compute property/topic effect ratio from true logits.
Activations of the query notes and of extra template pairs (hashtag, bullet, exclamation; second background) to estimate per-latent cue and topic shifts and the latent-captured fraction.
Per-latent contribution ranking from template-note shifts with sign rule and topic caps (first selection).
Read peak tokens of leading latents to confirm they fire on '#', '!' and line-start dashes.
Re-rank by corpus-regression shifts, compare budget splits for probe 0 and ceilings, settle 11 hashtag + 5 bullet latents and 16 exclamation latents.
Mean-ablation on sample notes: captured shift between label groups, saturation with 1/16/30 exclamation latents and 11/16/25 hashtag latents; bullet sweep could not run.
Build answer, check regex balanced accuracy against detectors on corpus, submit.

per_probe.conclusion: two cues: hashtag line and bulleted lines
per_probe.procedure: Hashtag had the largest corpus-regression effect; its logit-space dependence was well above 0.3. Bullet sat near 0.16, so a 2x2 knitting/astronomy x prose/bullet true-logit test was run, giving a ratio about 0.35, so it was added. Latents: gradient x corpus shift for each cue, same sign as total, per-latent topic contribution under 10% of a ~4.7 topic scale; 11 for hashtag and 5 for bullet after comparing splits. Peak tokens of leading latents were read; sample ablation checked the captured shift. Regexes '#\w+' and '(?m)^- ', checked against the detectors on corpus.

All confounded properties had logit-space dependence at or below about 0.07 after the topic effect was re-estimated from the sample label coefficient minus confound contributions; non-confounded properties served as calibration. Largest property effect would need implausible amplification to reach 0.3, so none.
per_probe.quote: **Probe 1**: max betaP_s=0.77 (bullet), needs implausible ×4 amplification to reach cue threshold → **none**

per_probe.procedure: Same logit-space dependence estimate; all confounded properties stayed at or below about 0.09 (largest was the P.S. line). The initial activation-space estimate had flagged P.S. as borderline, but the logit-space topic scale removed it. Answered none.

Exclamation was the only borderline property (about 0.16) in logit space. A 2x2 astronomy/running x period/exclamation true-logit test gave a ratio about 0.42, confirming it. Latent-captured fraction measured from activations of the same notes. 16 latents ranked by gradient x corpus shift with same-sign and topic filters; peak tokens checked; ablation with 1, 16 and 30 latents showed the gain flattening. Regex '!'.

caveats: Gradient/activation arrays were saved as files in the session; the API is assumed to return arrays directly. The probe-0 topic scale 4.7 was a hand-chosen number; the probe-3 topic scale came from the factorial. Intermediate selection variants (template-only ranking, dual-sign rule, 6/8% caps, split comparisons) are compressed into abandoned functions. The final answer step applied only the 10% per-latent cap, not the cumulative cap of earlier variants. The bullet size sweep failed and was skipped. Exact template sentences in the factorial notes are approximated.
